title: Is it safe to go back inside?
scenario: After the earthquake, deciding whether to re-enter your house or building. Safe re-entry, going back in for belongings.
steps: Stay out until you have looked over the building from outside. Aftershocks can occur without warning and can bring a weakened building down.

Check for structural damage: large cracks in walls or foundation, leaning walls, a sagging roof or floor, or the building shifted off its foundation. Any of these — do not enter, and get a professional inspection.
If you smell gas or hear hissing, stay out and follow the gas leak guidance.
If the building looks sound, enter briefly and carefully: sturdy shoes, flashlight (not candles), and someone outside who knows you went in.
Watch for broken glass, fallen objects overhead, and damaged wiring.
Leave immediately if you hear creaking or feel any shaking.
do_not: Do not use candles, matches, or lighters inside after a quake.
Do not turn utilities back on yourself if you suspect damage.
